Flow.description: ALF-RS-04: rolls per-item approval decisions up to the parent Appraisal's own AF_ApprovalStatus__c. Fires on an AppraisalItem's AF_ApprovalStatus__c reaching Approved or Rejected (RecordAfterSave, Update, ISCHANGED). Business rule (user-confirmed, verbatim): "reject wins immediately, don't wait" - if the item that just changed is Rejected, the parent Appraisal is set to Rejected right away, regardless of any sibling items still Pending. If the item that just changed is Approved, this queries ALL sibling AppraisalItems under the same AppraisalId EXCLUDING any that are Approved or Rejected already-consistent - specifically it looks for any sibling that is NOT Approved (i.e. still Pending, or blank); if none are found, every item is Approved and the parent Appraisal is set to Approved. If any sibling is still Pending, the parent Appraisal is left untouched (stays whatever it currently shows, typically Pending, until all items resolve). A Rejected sibling is excluded from the "not yet" wait state deliberately: if a sibling were already Rejected, the Rejected branch above would already have fired the immediate-reject on a prior transaction, so this Approved-branch query only needs to watch for Pending/blank stragglers, not Rejected ones (defensive: even if reached, this never overrides an already-Rejected parent since it only writes Approved when literally zero non-Approved siblings remain, which excludes a Rejected sibling by definition of it not being Approved). Writing to Appraisal.AF_ApprovalStatus__c here is what re-triggers the EXISTING, already-working Appraisal-level AF_FL_Appraisal_ApprovalApproved / AF_FL_Appraisal_ApprovalRejected flows (both still fire on ISCHANGED(Appraisal.AF_ApprovalStatus__c) reaching Approved/Rejected) - this flow deliberately does NOT duplicate owner-reassignment or rep/Contact email notification, since those already happen correctly at the Appraisal level once this flow's write lands. Verified live 2026-09-09: a same-transaction reject on one item produces exactly one Appraisal update, one ProcessInstance-independent field change, and the existing Appraisal-level rejected flow fires exactly once (one EmailMessage, one owner reassignment) - not duplicated. Real feature added 2026-09-09: now also drives the parent Appraisal's standard Status field (Automotive Cloud's own picklist: Initial Valuation/Visit Scheduled/Under Approval/Completed/Withdrawn) and keeps AF_TradeInOutcome__c consistent with the approval outcome. Any item reaching Pending now also fires this flow (previously only Approved/Rejected did), setting Status=Under Approval. On Rejected, Status reverts to Initial Valuation (ready for the Used Car Team to re-evaluate and resubmit, per AF_FL_AppraisalItem_EvaluationComplete/EvaluationSubmit's resubmission support) and AF_TradeInOutcome__c resets to In Progress. CORRECTED 2026-09-09 (real user feedback): on Approved, only AF_ApprovalStatus__c=Approved and AF_TradeInOutcome__c=Accepted are set automatically — Status is deliberately NOT auto-advanced to Completed here anymore (an earlier version of this flow did that). The Sales Rep now sets Status=Completed themselves once they've actually closed out the trade-in with the customer, since "Approved" (the valuation is cleared) and "Completed" (the rep has finished the transaction) are genuinely different moments the rep needs control over. AF_VR_Appraisal_StatusOutcomeConsistency only blocks the wrong direction (Status=Completed without Outcome=Accepted) to allow this transient Approved-but-not-yet-Completed state. LFRDN-756 (2026-09-28): Set_Appraisal_Approved no longer sets AF_TradeInOutcome__c = Accepted. Approval only clears the valuation; the customer's decision is recorded on the item, and AF_FL_AppraisalItem_RollupOutcomeToAppraisal derives the header outcome from it (header stays In Progress until then).
